ai.summary: Alibaba said its Qwen model will power Apple Intelligence features—including Siri and Writing Tools—in mainland China. A developer beta is expected November 4, with a wider launch planned for December, subject to Apple’s rollout plans.
ai.title: Alibaba's Qwen and Apple Intelligence team up

ai.summary: Google said it successfully ran an AI model on a satellite and received a response on Earth, using an onboard TPU. The test is part of Project Suncatcher, an effort to explore the technical feasibility of computing in space; Google has not announced a commercial service.
ai.title: Google Just Made AI Talk From Space for the First Time Ever

ai.summary: Quad foreign ministers said they intend to provide more than $85 million in assistance to expand access to trusted AI across the Indo-Pacific. They also announced plans to identify semiconductor and AI supply-chain vulnerabilities.
ai.title: Quad to step up cooperation in AI, critical minerals

ai.summary: China’s proposed export controls would restrict transfers of certain AI models, expertise and related technologies while generally allowing overseas customers to access Chinese AI through websites and cloud services. The draft proposals remain open for public comment through November 15.
ai.title: China’s new export curbs draw a line around its AI crown jewels

ai.summary: AIB’s roundup reports that five major technology companies expect up to $828 billion in AI-related capital spending in 2026. The spending plans underscore the scale of the industry’s investment in computing and data-center infrastructure.
ai.title: Latest AI News — Global AI News and Industry Trends, Summarized Daily

ai.summary: A newsletter roundup reports that Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic backed a shared robots.txt control for AI-training opt-outs, announced by Google on October 30. The proposal would let website operators signal that their content should not be used to train generative AI systems.
ai.title: The 6:30 — AI's trillion-dollar reckoning: spending fears, supply fights, and a robots.txt truce

quantum.summary: Researchers demonstrated quantum-LDPC surgery on Quantinuum’s H2-2 trapped-ion processor, selectively measuring one logical qubit in a two-qubit code block using seven ancillas. Repeating the measurement across three syndrome rounds reduced the observed error rate below 0.26%; the distance-3 code and offline decoding mean this is an early hardware demonstration, not yet a scalable fault-tolerant system.
quantum.title: Seven borrowed qubits read one logical qubit out of a block of two, and the other one came through at 0.21 percent

quantum.summary: Researchers report a bosonic encoding scheme intended to let an oscillator protect a qubit while sensing weak external forces. Their analysis and superconducting-circuit benchmarks suggest memory errors can be suppressed while retaining state-independent readout, though the report is based on a research paper rather than a demonstrated commercial capability.
quantum.title: Researchers Bound Memory Error To Gamma Raised To R Plus One

quantum.summary: The NAKO framework benchmarks neutral-atom quantum compilers against lower bounds for measures such as atom movement and Rydberg stages, and helps identify sources of inefficiency. In reported tests, diagnosis-guided changes to one compiler cut mean atom movement by 78.9% across five matched circuits.
quantum.title: Meet NAKO, A Benchmarking Framework For Evaluating And Diagnosing Neutral-Atom Quantum Compilers

quantum.summary: Quantum Art researchers proposed an algorithm that prepares quantum states directly on the physical dispersion relations relevant to wave propagation, rather than searching a much larger solution space. The claimed potential for very large simulations is prospective: the work is a preprint, not evidence that current quantum hardware has run those calculations at the described scale.
quantum.title: Quantum algorithm targets wave simulations beyond the reach of supercomputers

quantum.summary: A hybrid approach combines variational quantum algorithms with adiabatic quantum computing to train entanglement-detection models. The report says it reaches systems of up to 25 qubits, but the available coverage does not establish a practical advantage over classical methods.
quantum.title: Researchers Train Algorithms To Detect Entanglement Using Quantum Computing

quantum.summary: IBM introduced a Quantum Safe software suite intended to help organizations identify vulnerable cryptography and plan migrations to post-quantum standards. The announcement is about cybersecurity preparation for future quantum threats, rather than a new quantum-computing machine or capability.
quantum.title: IBM Launches Tools for Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
